title: Minimum Sum of Mountain Triplets II
summary: Given an array nums, find the minimum sum of indices (i, j, k) where i < j < k, and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k].
statement: Given an array nums, find the minimum sum of indices (i, j, k) where i < j < k, and nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k]. If no such triplet exists, return -1.
constraints: nums contains at least three positive integers.
Choose i<j<k with both nums[i] and nums[k] strictly smaller than the middle value nums[j].
Return the minimum three-value sum, or -1 when no mountain triplet exists.
hints: For each middle index, only the smallest value on each side can minimize a valid sum.
Precompute suffix minima and maintain a running prefix minimum.
When both side minima are strictly below the middle, update their three-value sum.
Any valid middle is improved or matched by replacing its endpoints with the side minima, so testing every middle is exhaustive and optimal.
editorial: Any valid middle is improved or matched by replacing its endpoints with the side minima, so testing every middle is exhaustive and optimal.

tests.explanation: Values one, five, and three form the minimum mountain sum nine.
Values four, seven, and two form the minimum sum thirteen.
